title: Assessment of AI-Assisted Ultrasound in DDH
official: Assessment of the Diagnostic Accuracy of an Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Ultrasound Device by Novice Users for Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip AI/ML
summary:
Developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) is a condition in which a baby's hip joint does not develop normally. Ultrasound is commonly used to assess the hips of young infants for DDH, but these examinations usually require trained ultrasound staff and specialist interpretation.

The purpose of this study is to determine whether a handheld ultrasound device combined with artificial intelligence (AI) can be used by non-specialist health care personnel to obtain and assess ultrasound images of infant hips. Infants attending the Baby Hip Clinic at The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids) will undergo their usual clinical ultrasound as part of their standard care. They will also have an additional research ultrasound performed using the handheld device.

Researchers will compare the research ultrasound with the standard clinical ultrasound. The study will assess the quality of the images obtained using the handheld device and compare the AI-assisted assessment with the diagnosis from the standard ultrasound and assessments made by experienced reviewers. The research ultrasound and AI results will not be used to make treatment decisions for participating infants.

interventions.name: Handheld Point-of-Care Hip Ultrasound with AI-Assisted Analysis

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Infants referred to the SickKids Orthopaedic Baby Hip Clinic for possible or confirmed DDH.
* Infants aged 0-6 months.
* Parent/guardian willing and able to provide consent on behalf of the infant.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Infants with known or suspected neuromuscular, collagen, chromosomal or lower-extremity congenital abnormalities or syndromic-associated hip abnormalities.
* Infants that have already started treatment.
* Parent/guardian not willing and able to provide consent on behalf of the infant.
